history.dynasty: Kalyana Chalukya, 12th century origins (documented in the Karnataka District Gazetteer: Bidar); modified during the Bahmani Sultanate era
history.summary: The Papnash Shiva Temple is a 12th-century Shiva temple in a green valley on the edge of Bidar, built in the Kalyana Chalukya idiom with later Bahmani-era arches and motifs, and laid out in the trikuta (three-shrine) plan. Its name comes from the natural spring 'Papnash' (destroyer of sins) that feeds the pond and stepped kalyani in front of the temple; devotees believe a dip washes away sins. Local legend holds that the lingam was installed by Lord Rama on his return from Lanka. NOTE: some recent web articles attach precise claims to the temple (e.g. specific PRASHAD-scheme funding figures) that were not independently verified — stick to the gazetteer and established press coverage. CSV NOTE: the CSV's 'state' column wrongly holds the town name 'Bidar' — the temple is in the state of Karnataka.

name: Papnash Shiva Temple
town_description: Bidar is a historic town in northeastern Karnataka, once the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, known for its fort, the Mahmud Gawan madrasa and Bidri metalwork. It lies about 120-140 km from Hyderabad and is the district headquarters of Bidar district.

travel.airport: Bidar Airport has no scheduled commercial services; the nearest operational airport is Hyderabad, approx. 130-140 km.
travel.railway: Bidar railway station, a few kilometres from the temple complex.
travel.road: On the outskirts of Bidar in a valley, a short auto or taxi ride from the city; Papnash lake lies beside the temple.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. Maha Shivaratri is the grand celebration and draws the biggest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daytime darshan; exact opening hours are not published in the sources consulted — verify locally before visiting.
